item.title: Keeping Locum or Part-time Healthcare Professionals Up-to-date with Clinical Practices

attempt.title: Keeping Locum or Part-time Healthcare Professionals Up-to-date with Clinical Practices
attempt.what_it_is: Keeping Locum or Part-time Healthcare Professionals Up-to-date with Clinical Practices

sections.label: Staff training and professional education
sections.summary: Licensees must ensure staff are properly onboarded and trained, and registered professionals must keep up with standards and CPE.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Licensees of healthcare institutions also bear a responsibility to ensure that their staff, including part-timers or locums, are properly onboarded and adequately trained to perform the tasks that they are assigned, through establishing appropriate protocols and processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Professional Boards require that all registered healthcare professionals keep up-to-date on current standards of care and treatment, and participate in Continuing Professional Education (CPE) programmes or activities to renew their Practising Certificates.

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccination error reporting rules
sections.summary: Additional regulations set eligibility, dosage, emergency management and incident reporting, requiring providers to report errors to MOH within three hours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Specifically, for COVID-19 vaccination, we issued additional regulations to stipulate the prevailing eligibility criteria, the dilution and administration of the recommended dosage for each vaccine, the management of emergencies and incident reporting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In the event of any vaccine administration errors and medical emergencies following vaccination, the vaccination providers are required to report to MOH no later than three hours after the incident.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The providers are also required to inform the patients immediately when a vaccination error has occurred, provide appropriate immediate care and then, monitor the patients' health with daily calls for the next seven days to ensure their well-being.

sections.label: ProHealth investigation and vaccination dosing errors
sections.summary: MOH is investigating ProHealth Medical Group, and as of 26 September 2022, 11 overdosing and 119 underdosing cases occurred among about 16 million doses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOH is currently investigating ProHealth Medical Group about the incident on 15 September 2022 and will take appropriate enforcement actions if there are any regulatory breaches.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As of 26 September 2022, out of approximately 16 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines administered, there had been 11 persons affected by overdosing and 119 persons affected by underdosing of the vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Of these, seven were children, aged between five and 11, who did not have any adverse reactions.
